dedupe_keys.name: economic benefits of the global positioning system rti international for nist 2019

description: This economic appraisal, prepared by RTI International for the National Institute of Standards and Technology and released in June 2019, estimates the benefits that private-sector use of the Global Positioning System has brought to the United States and the losses a long outage would cause. It measured ten industries (agriculture, electricity, finance, location-based services, mining, maritime, oil and gas, surveying, telecommunications and telematics) and estimated about $1.4 trillion of economic benefits since GPS became available in the 1980s. It also analysed a 30-day GPS outage, which could cost roughly $1 billion a day, rising to as much as $45 billion if it struck agriculture during planting season, and noted that impacts vary with industry, season and the stage of the outage. Coverage: the United States, 1984 to 2017 for benefits, plus outage scenarios. Format and access: free PDF report from NIST, RTI, GPS.gov and the Office of Space Commerce, with a summary presentation. Caveats: estimates rely on literature, interviews and industry models; the outage analysis assumes users adapt over time, which some commentators argued understates the risk; public-sector and military benefits are excluded. Simulation uses: cost inputs for hazard scenarios of GPS loss from space weather, jamming or system faults, cascading-failure analysis across dependent sectors, and investment cases for complementary positioning and timing. Related records: the London Economics studies give UK estimates, and the US DOT complementary PNT demonstration tested backups.
